items.title: Jon Hendricks — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The name 'Liza' appears only in the [INTERVIEWER]'s turn quoting a poem ('Liza, Liza, bless the Lord...'). The interviewee does not mention Liza, nor does he respond to the name specifically, only continuing his narrative about poetry.

ctx.x: – he wrote in the Shakespearean mode. He wrote in the Shelley and Byron mode. He wrote that poem about art and love. It’s gorgeous. But when he wrote in the slavery manner, the idiomatic manner of the slaves, he was superb, like that line where he talks about going . . .

“Liza, Liza, bless the Lord. Don’t you know these days is broad? If you don’t get up you scamp, there’ll be trouble in this camp. Think I gonna let you sleep?” It goes on. I remember my grandmother’s very favorite poems.
I like that line where he says, “They set down to some unskun coon.” Unskun. Of course skun is the past tense of skin.
